html:
The Palyku, also written Bailgu, are an Aboriginal people of the eastern Pilbara in Western Australia, in hill country between the upper Fortescue River and Nullagine.

Their neighbours on the map include the Nyamal to the north, the Banyjima to the west and Martu desert peoples to the east. Like other Pilbara peoples, they lived from hunting, seeds and the waterholes of the ranges. Pastoral stations and later gold diggings at Nullagine reached their country from the late 1800s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Palyku, also written Bailgu, are an Aboriginal people of the eastern Pilbara in Western Australia, in hill country between the upper Fortescue River and Nullagine.
